title: Where are the keyboard shortcuts
body:
Frustrating and lacking basic keyboard shortcut support

Google Sheets is incredibly frustrating to use if you’re accustomed to working efficiently with keyboard shortcuts on a Mac. Shortcuts that are quick and intuitive are absent, which makes editing and navigating spreadsheets unnecessarily slow.

For a productivity tool, having reliable keyboard shortcuts should be a basic feature. Constantly having to reach for the mouse or remember different key combinations completely disrupts the workflow.

Google Sheets has plenty of useful features, but the poor and inconsistent iPad keyboard shortcut experience seriously hurts its usability. If you’re an iPad user who relies heavily on keyboard shortcuts, be prepared for a frustrating experience.

title: Horrible layout
body:
The recent layout update has made the app much harder to use. Moving the formatting shortcuts completely behind the "A" button at the top instead of keeping them accessible right on the bottom bar like before adds unnecessary steps to basic tasks. 

It is incredibly frustrating to have to go into a whole different area just to add a row. It now takes three separate taps just to add a single row. For every single row added, the entire popup menu disappears, meaning you can no longer just spam the add button to insert multiple rows quickly like you used to. 

Furthermore, users used to have immediate access to essential tools right on the main screen. The background color of a cell, bold, italics, underline, and the text alignment position within the cell were all easily accessible. Now, all of these features are blocked under a completely separate section rather than being right there. The previous design was much more efficient for mobile editing.

title: The Google Sheets app should be a full workforce version, instead of a fancy app which lacks major f
body:
Google Sheets on the desktop is an absolute powerhouse for productivity, but the mobile app feels like a "lite" version designed only for viewing, not for actual heavy lifting. If Google wants this to be a serious workforce tool, they need to stop prioritizing the "fancy," minimalist mobile UI and actually port over the functional power of the desktop version. • Missing Core Features: You can’t bulk-add rows or columns efficiently, and major data tools like Pivot Table editing, Conditional Formatting rules, and Data Validation (dropdown) management are either hidden or completely non-existent.
• Poor Navigation: Navigating frozen columns or large datasets is a nightmare compared to the desktop experience. The "fancy" touch interface often gets in the way of precision when selecting specific cell ranges.  
• No Apps Script Support: For a "workforce" app, the lack of ability to run or even view basic scripts on mobile is a huge bottleneck. I shouldn't have to wait until I’m back at a computer to trigger a simple automation.
• Formatting Limitations: Basic things like custom fill colors or advanced chart customization are stripped out. It makes the app feel like a toy rather than a professional spreadsheet tool.

title: Very good - but Google could make it super
body:
This app has amazing capabilities, and a few silly defects. 

+ WAYYYY more stable than Excel on mobile. 

+ You can share full-featured spreadsheets in real time. On my iPhone I can correct data right next to the cell my niece is editing on a Windows desktop hundreds of miles away. 

+ Really powerful: even on the mobile version you can create SQL-like queries of spreadsheet or external data, and useful charts. 

+ Super easy data input from Google forms for repetitive stuff. 

- Some major browser-version features — edit-triggered routines, for  example, and modifying protection — aren’t available on the mobile version. 

- iOS app is missing many useful features available on Android 

- Charts are bizarrely primitive on all versions. Apparently, Google has decided to leave this function up to Microsoft and dedicated charting apps.

title: Unreliable
body:
I use the app in only one place. My phone. Yet somehow my data keeps suddenly shifting back to data from several days ago, and loses everything between now and then. And it's not even a complicated sheet. Just rows of dates with bill amounts, what I need for that day, and what I ended with for that day. The next day is calculated on my minimum daily needs, and continues down the line throughout the days of the year. I'm constantly getting hit with being father behind than I thought I was because I've entered this days numbers onto where I was several days ago. 

Last night I closed out my numbers for the 15th of February. Hit the check in the upper corner and got back out. I do this every day. 

Now tonight, the 16th I went to put in my numbers, and the sheet was back to the 13th!! 

This keeps happening. I have NOTHING else using this sheet. 

I'm going to have to switch to a different spreadsheet. I can't afford getting hot with financial surprises like this. And this happens frequently. 2-3 times per month, if not more. 

If it were just yesterdays data, then maybe I can understand that maybe it was me and I somehow didn't close the day out properly. But when it's 3, 4, or even more days back? Days that I've already filled in? No. This is not on my end. 

Now if you'll excuse me, I have to go try to reconstruct my weekend... 😡

title: A Good App, Mostly
body:
Considering myself experienced in the use of Excel, the Sheets functionality feels familiar. That said, I have found missing functionality within the first week of use. Specifically, the ability to customize number format is missing. I sought to change the available x.yz type (integer with two decimal places) format to only one digit after the decimal point. I could not find it within the app, and consulting Google pointed me to “Custom Format”, which doesn’t exist in the app. More dogged search eventually revealed that customization of that number format is not available on mobile. Irritating. 

Some of the data entry methods are annoyingly obtuse. Part of that is implementation, and part of that is inherent from being on a mobile device. Examples are two-fold use of the same “underlined A” to signify Formatting at the top but text color formatting at the bottom, and the switch-to-text-from-numbers placed within the spreadsheet field rather than the expected bottom of the screen somewhere. 

iPhone 11, iOS 18.6.2, 3 Jan 2026
(hesitant to move to iOS 26.X…)

title: #1 Must-Delete app from iPad
body: After using Google Sheets in a desktop browser for years, I thought it would be simple to migrate to an iPad. Well, if you have super-simple sheets, maybe. All of the most powerful features are gone. Conditional formatting? Gone. Selecting disjoint ranges? Hah. Copy then Paste values, formulas, or formats only? Nope. Find and replace in formulas with RE2 regular expressions? No chance. Macros and functions? Triggers? Haha, what even are those? Keyboard shortcuts? Sigh. (And yes, iPad folks do use external keyboards.) Adding insult to injury, it’s nearly impossible to open a sheet in any browser on iPad (clearly Google hates Safari) and if you try…it keeps jumping you to the app. Deleted the app? Sends you to the App Store. Almost lying that the app is “better” when it is so fundamentally deficient. And if you manage to open the sheet in a browser, which you HAVE TO for all the stuff I listed above, then you’ll lose a 2-3 rows of your sheet to a message telling you to switch to the app. Good grief. If you have stupidly simple tabular data, go ahead, use this app. Or just use the Notes app, since it’s probably just as good.

title: Suggestions to Improve Google Sheets Home Page Interface
body:
Dear Google Team,

I’d love to suggest a few ways to improve the usability of the Google Sheets home page and make it more aligned with the flexibility of Google Docs:
	1.	Organizational Sorting
The homepage would benefit from sorting options similar to Google Docs—by time last opened, alphabetical order, or owner. That layout makes navigation far easier.
	2.	Document Density & Layout Options
Currently, only a limited number of Sheets are visible at once. It would be helpful to allow users to adjust the size of document thumbnails or switch to a denser view to fit more on the page, especially for users managing a large number of files.
	3.	Color-Coding at a Glance
Allowing users to assign color labels or background tints to their Sheets on the home screen would help visually separate different themes or projects—at a glance.
	4.	Cleaner Iconography
The green Excel-style cross on the bottom left of each document isn’t necessary and feels outdated. A simpler, more consistent “Sheets” label would improve clarity and reduce visual clutter.
	5.	Smarter Previews
If users have multiple files with similar formats or titles, it becomes difficult to distinguish between them just by looking at the preview thumbnail. A customizable or smarter preview system could really help.

Overall, Google Sheets is powerful, but the interface could be much more sophisticated and customizable—especially at the file management level. I often find myself wondering if a more advanced version is coming, but the homepage experience hasn’t evolved much over the years.

Thanks for your continued innovation and for considering this feedback.

Warmly,
Kendall

title: Lacks critical functionality
body: Sheets cannot be used for any serious data analysis and manipulation and lacks seriously critical functionality needed by anyone doing any legitimate work. For example, I cannot find any way to convert a file and save it as a CSV using the mobile app, and my Jupyter notebooks/python environments on my iPad require UTF-8 encoded files to be uploaded and used by my programs (aka, a CSV). Sheets needs to have these basic functionalities added to it if Google expects their app to be used and trusted by people who are trying to use a great Cloud supported, free spreadsheet alternative for serious projects. In other words, try to be like Excel as much as possible.

title: My Volunteer participation at Darshan
body:
I have been a volunteer for Isha Customer Service since my Shambhavi consecration in 2022. 
This time I considered to participate as an InfoBooth volunteer at Sadhguru’s Initiation Day Darshan, and the days preceding. 
The entire experience was exceptionally elevating. 
The Abode and preparations for its annaversary during these days lit up an energy like never felt before. The inpouring of hundreds of meditators and visitors to touch the Shiva Linga, consecrated by Sadhguru brought ecstasy of experience. 
I fell into its depth and energy more than a few times. 
And the rest of my days here brought another selfless experience, inclusiveness. 
My desire to serve any and everyone who came by my Info booth revived my inner longing for the experience of connection and a touch of love that was radiating over this consecrated land and it’s adjacent community. 
I met so many people, with radiating smiles and soft hearts. Asking so many questions and receiving answers, as best I could, that made them feel Sadhguru’s immense love and his presence. 
I had the opportunity to lead some through signing up for the valued InnerEngineering course created by Sadhguru- the cherished program that is truly transformative, that brings one closer to True Being. 
Some asked about Sadhguru’s enticing poetry and where to buy Adiyogi tee shirts. Others interested in the hikes to the waterfall and enquiry about how to become part of this Living space so that they can enroll their children into the best place for education and wellness. A few other young people came, connected, and asked about how to become long time volunteers. 
I love connecting and communicating with people since I trained in InnerEngineering Ambassadorship, to help bring even a drop of spirituality to people through a practice. And being a volunteer for InnerEngineering customer service helped me guide them from experiences I gained to taking the course and seeing for themselves, through the practice of Shambhavi, the inclusiveness that it brings. 
Truly, I felt a sense of boundless expanse. 
Just being in this event begins to confirm and seal the reason I had decided to give up everything in California and move here just two weeks ago. 
I am beginning to see the light that penetrates and the energy that radiates- the grace of my Guru, in my life.

title: Mobile App User Interface.
body:
Now, I’m a long time user and fan of most spreadsheet software, even if I don’t use it. But, I’ve recently stopped using a computer for unavoidable reasons I won’t go into. (What is the point of a larger bulkier computer when I’m basically told I have to carry one with me, that supersedes the base purpose me having a phone in the first place?) 

Now, I use(d) Excel primarily, and was told nigh endlessly about how good Sheets was. So, I have been working prior to switching to a mobile as my work station (on a paying job, no less) in Sheets. Only to find out, that none of the actual infrastructure that allows for any legitimate complexity (aside from formulas), is accessible. I can’t access any context menus, development, design, tables, data validation (which is paramount when dealing with simultaneously non-numerical and complex hierarchical Data). My work and experiences, suffer to the point, that I may as well know nothing more than ‘box make math’. 

Any real work is limited to manually parsing everything from the ground up. While you can make ‘Filters’, which is the analog to Tables (because all table have to be ‘Pivot’ style now), listing functions via the function icon to the data entry field while editing a cell, and the tool(?) bar host only some basic formatting functionality, is not viable for anyone who actually knows enough to use spreadsheet software. 

I can’t make named ranges for ease of reference, limit acceptable information within a cell or range, use scripts to facilitate operations not covered in functions, create menus, and other fun and useful things. What is the point of a mobile Sheets App as anything more than a viewer for files created on other mediums like Desktops and Laptops? 

Currently, I’m really put off by Google products, leaning into ease of use over functionality. I don’t mind ease of use. I don’t even mind the convenience. But, this App is ‘NOT’ Google Sheets. It is at -best- ‘Google Sheets Lite’ which is basically no different in functional accessibility than a PDF reader. At -Worst- It’s a misleading representation of software, that rides on its name to lure people into using it, instead of the complex system it portends to be. 

I did try accessing the sheets on my phone’s browser, even requesting desktop websites in hopes of proper functionality. No luck there, either. All relevant solutions with regard to my situation call for a laptop or desktop exclusively. I am profoundly disappointed in my experience here, and currently wouldn’t recommend this to anyone considering it for convenience, unless their experience and needs were novice. Even then, I would warn them. 

Hopefully, these are things that can and will be addressed and corrected for. As it is, Sheets on mobile devices appears by all accounts to be a waste of time. Please tell me there’s hope in the future. I’m losing money because your app lacks functionality.

title: The most glitch-ridden of all Google apps
body:
I use Google Sheets every day, and every day I force quit the app 3-5 times because of inexplicable glitches and bugs. That has remained constant across the past year, through many app updates and versions. If it were a random app from a small developer, I would chalk it up to normal cost of doing business, but this is Alphabet—if any company on earth should solve bugs, it is them.

About 10% of the time when open a sheet, I see no fields populated, only highlighted colors. I have to force quit the app and reload to see the data. Most frequently, there are glitches when you try to toggle quickly between editing multiple fields. I often cannot edit a field after selecting it, or close the editor after entering data. In both cases, I have to force quit and reload the app.

Again, it’s a powerful and useful app, but it feels like freeware somebody made in their garage, not a mainstay Google product. After so long, these should be high-priority fixes.

title: Best Real-time collaboration BUT
body:
Overall decent excel replacement only from a basic feature standpoint. 

The two most tedious things I find with sheets: 
1. the inability to add more detailed formatting without memorizing key commands (like bullets or even just new lines in merged cells).
2. Number of clicks. Something that saves me SO much time when formatting excel is that the toolbars remembers my last choice (like borders). Every time I want to do a border in sheets I MUST use 2 clicks. This doubles my work, time, and wrist strain.

title: Poor Man’s Workspace
body:
Everything I have, I’ve gained through my own labor and experience, starting after I graduated highschool and moved out at 18, and entered workforce with no skills that didn’t involve breaking a sweat. As the years go on I’ve had to find more unconventional ways to worm my way into the business world.
I have a $40 Chromebook from wal mart and access to Docs, Sheets, Drive, Gmail, etc. without paying a penny more. Whatever negative things might be said about the apps, I’ll say they’re underrated for pure value and accessibility. 
I’m extremely blessed and thankful to live in this generation; I could be stuck driving trucks for a small business or cutting grass for an even smaller one (like I was, 7 days a week) but now I’m making plans to start my own business and using Google’s tools to build up a more useful skillset.

title: Why bother?
body:
I’m not sure why Google has bothered to keep this app up on the app store.  It is missing almost all of the core functionality (and functions!) that are necessary for people trying to do basic data analysis.

If all you need is cells and rows and to do some basic formulas, it’s fine.  But basically all of the advanced functions in the tool bars are missing.  Literally every menu item is missing.  And doing basic procedures such as sorting (which is a core piece of spreadsheet functionality) is clunky to use.

You are far better off simply opening a browser window on your iPad and logging into Google sheets that way.  It’s the only way to actually get the full Sheets experience on iPad.  And it’s totally frustrating because it’s not as if the Google version on Android lacks these features or that Google of all companies is lacking the programmers to make it an actually full fledged app.

This is highly disappointing as I’m using Corsera to learn Data Analytics and my iPad as my primary learning/computing device for this purpose.  And there is this intentional road block in the way that simply doesn’t need to be there.

title: Why can’t I make a table here?????
body:
To preface, I am an Excel girly so I’m already biased. I have to use Sheets for work, hence the move. Since college, I had to sell my laptop and only use an iPad. Works pretty well for most things except some mobile apps… including, you guessed it, this one. 

Scene: I log into Google Sheets and click ‘New Spreadsheet’. Simple. I write in my heading. Done. Then I go to search for the ‘Table’ tab. You know, the one that pretty much every spreadsheet platform has since that’s what spreadsheets are built for. Well, apparently this spreadsheet platform has decided to skimp out on those tables because I cannot find it ANYWHERE. I google “how to make tables in Google Sheets app”. All the results say to highlight the cell, make the border bigger, set fill color to yada yada- MANUALLY making the table. Sir, if I wanted to manually make a table I would write it out on my notepad from ECON 1010. No one has manually made a table since before Britney was free. 

I long for the ‘Table’ tab. Please bring her back. Until then, I will be manually making tables like the indentured servant I apparently am.

title: Missing Features
body:
There are so many features missing from the iOS App that I’m constantly switching to the full web-based version just to get one thing done, which wastes time.  It would be nice if there was a single help page with a matrix of ALL features and tells us what is in the web version vs the iOS app, so we can decide which one (web or app) to use.  It would be nice if that matrix told us exactly where each feature/button was located, and when it appears (some are context-specific). There should be a single button to switch in either direction (web to app, or app to web) and not have to find the documents again.

The Google help pages are constantly out of date with the app, describing buttons or processes that don’t exist or have been moved.

There is really no easy way for users to know when specific bugs are recognized by the Google dev team and when each bug is fixed, aside from trying the feature.

I DO like when functions are marked as “new”, which prompts me to explore them.  I’d also like an (optional) “changed” flag that links back to the change notices and bug fixes.

title: Minimizes Functionality the Browsers Offer
body:
I have no idea who is rating this app with so many 5 star ratings, but the app is outrageously clunky vs using it in a browser. For some reason, my sheets documents have been refusing to let me opt out of using the app so I attempted to use the app this morning.
1. Typing into a cell and using the left or right arrow doesn’t work
2. Highlighting a row to insert is a way too many step process
3. After finally highlighting cells to insert a row, clicking anywhere on the screen brings up the “cut, copy, paste” features even though I’m using command + c or command + x.
4. Command + d does not copy the value from the cell above like it does in the browser version
5. Format painter is non-existent?
The list goes on, but those browser features that aren’t available in the app that the browser prompts you to open every time you use sheets is enough to rate this app with a 1 star. It’s an infuriating app.

body:
EDIT: They have now added autocorrect. Except… not the standard autocorrect. No, that would be too simple. Best of all, it gives absolutely no sign that it’s going to change your word, and doesn’t actually change it until you’ve typed an addition sentence, and sometimes even hit enter to save the cell. How INSANE are these developers? Oh and most of the other problems… still exist. Only now you can’t use the dropdown data validation features that you’ve set up. 

Worst part is - they FORCE you to use this - you can’t use a browser.

Something as simple as typing into a cell doesn’t work! First of all, no autocorrect. But worse, you can’t edit anything without google making up some random new rules about how your keyboard works, like mandating all-caps so that you have to hit shift before EVERY LETTER to turn it off. By far my most frustrating experience each day. An absolute embarrassment that this experience is happening in 2018. title: My G Sheet helps my health & it’s FREE!
body: I am a type 2 diabetic with glaucoma & hereditary high cholesterol. I made a “health” sheet to track and average my blood glucose as my meter only gives a 2 week average. An A1c averages for around 3 months & it made sense to me to track for a longer average. Since I am considered in “remission”, I would not qualify for a CGM (continuous glucose meter). I also added a column on my “ health” sheet to track blood pressure measurements which I keep an eye on because of the glaucoma. The cholesterol sheet calculates my triglyceride to HDL ratio. I can also update & view my G sheets from my phone, tablet or laptop regardless of OS. And it’s FREE! Excel was my all time favorite, but I no longer need all that power as I don’t work in an office anymore. Thanks to the folks at Google I have a great way to help maintain my health! Thumbs way up for me!

title: Are other reviewers using the same app as me?
body:
UPDATE: I think it’s actually gotten worse. But what makes it ridiculously frustrating is that logging into the URL for sheets in a browser forces me to the app. Why would you want to force people to use such a horrible experience? I know the experience in the safari on ipad isn’t ideal but it’s exponentially better than the iOS Sheets app.

Original review:
I can’t imagine why anyone would review this positively unless maybe they’ve never used any spreadsheet program. Ever. Maybe not even a calculator. Excel at least feels like they know iPad exists. Sheets acts like all we want to do is view an occasional sheet from others. Menu bar disappears every time I edit a cell then reappears when I hit enter. Formatting options are hard to find. title: Google Sheets for IPad - Fundamentally Flawed
body: Google Sheets and other programs like it are flexible, able to be used for multiple purpose across many different fields. As such Google Sheets for IPAD may work fine for you but for my job and how I use it I spend more time hitting roadblocks and having to open my computer to accomplish tasks than I should. It leads to the essential question of why even have an app if it will be missing so many core features and have many more that are broken or flawed.  The most recent examples include freezing vertical columns doing the opposite of the intended function, the complete lack of in cell text formatting, the lack of advanced sorting features and the inability to open two windows of google sheets at the same time.  These are just the broken or missing features that have interrupted my workflow today, I am sure that more will occur in the future. With an app this unfinished I would look to Excel or Apple’s Numbers as alternatives if my work didn’t rely on GSuite for the sharing functionality. If the only reason a user continues to use an app is being locked into the ecosystem, it is not a good app. If you are able avoid Google Sheets and all other Google apps to avoid getting trapped in their ecosystem, especially if you plan to try and use your IPAD as a main work device.

title: Not mobile-friendly at all
body: I hate this app so much. I have been using it for more than two years, 2-3 hours a day to track my training, and it is always one of my largest headaches of the day. The offline mode is completely unreliable. I can be disconnected from wifi, using the app, lock my phone to do a set, unlock my phone, try to return to the app, and be unable to edit the worksheet I was just editing because I'm offline. 5 minutes later, it might magically work again. The selecting and editing tool, ugh. 4/5 times I edit a cell, I confirm the edit, then somehow the cell highlight gets dragged over additional cells and I have to make my edit again. This happens at least 2-3 times a training session depending on how closely I am tracking my session.   Maybe this is a mobile memory limitation, but if I open 2 other apps, sheets completely loses which project I had open and which sheet. This is specifically annoying for my use case given I have separate sheets for each training week, which means they all look the same. When this happens, it's not unusual for me to forget to switch to the correct sheet after re-selecting my project, and update my session tracking numbers there. This means I often overwrite the wrong week, which means at least one week isn't accurate in tracking my program progress. Alternating between the alphabet keyboard and number keypad does not work. You can click the bubble to switch, but the keyboard will not switch until you've begun typing. I need to find another app, plainly. This app is not mobile-friendly on any account, and I find that for every operation I need to do in the app, there is something that makes it incredibly annoying with a high chance of having to redo it.

Dear Google,

I really do like all of your productivity software—Sheets, Docs, etc.  they are extremely underpowered for iPadPro.  IPadPro apps should be just like their desktop versions.

Since I have the app, and I like having the app because of the multitasking functionality, I have limited functions and options available.

I beg Google to update their apps for iPadPro users.  Microsoft has done that for their Office Suite and their apps run really well.  I really don’t want to support MS any more than I have to though.  Please update your iPadPro apps to work just like desktop software.

Very sincerely,
Brian

title: Poor functionality
body: I can use command-a to select all of the text in a cell, but I cannot use command-i to make text italic. I cannot select and edit text within a cell, only in the bar on the bottom, thus making it incredibly inefficient. For someone doing qualitative research without access to Nvivo, spreadsheets are an important tool. While sheets on laptops and desktops is a viable rival for excel, and google’s ability for teams to simultaneously edit sheets is unchallenged, the mobile app makes it nearly impossible for me to get my work accomplished using my tablet with keyboard attachment. Why lug around my laptop when I can bring my brand new tablet that handles everything else so well? Google - get the functionality of this app on par with the sheets browser experience. Do not recommend using this app for mobile. Stick to the browser, or use a different program entirely.

title: A useful but flawed app
body: Overall Google Sheets on an iPhone is a frustrating experience. Everything seems to work, though some functions are buried deep in a messy menu. The biggest problem I have is when editing text that has already been entered into a cell. You are brought to the end of the text that is already present. If there are many characters and you want to edit something at the beginning of the cell, you must scroll all.the.way back to the beginning with the clunky space bar scroll function in iOS. This usually results in autocorrect adding spaces to existing words and then via the erroneous magic of autocorrect you have nonsensical words marooned in your cell. Once you have reached your scrolling destination and start typing, you can’t see what you’ve typed. You are shown only the characters that are entered after the new text. This is very annoying and it has made me reach for my laptop instead of my phone when I want to work with a spreadsheet on Google Sheets.

I tried the “Help and Feedback” tab within the app and Googled it....both said these options were in a specific spot and they aren’t. I found both in Google Docs, but not Google Sheets. title: Dear Google- GIVE US THE FULL SOFTWARE!
body:
UPDATE:

That’s right, there is a new update to GOOGLE sheets. It’s now “Compatible” with iPad iOS/13. What’s really cool about the new iOS update is that Safari is the actual desktop version (no more mobile version). This means that it should allow me to access the online version of google sheets, right? Wrong. Because Google forces you to go to the app version EVERY TIME!

You know what’s not in the Sheets update? The desktop version! If iOS can support a desktop version of Safari then Google can make a Google Sheets that is the full version on iOS. Even Tim Cook has stated; “iPad Pro and this new iOS for iPad is so iPad can replace Laptops.”

Get it together, GOOGLE!

____________________________________________________________

I am an iPad Pro user. I love this tablet. I use this thing for video, graphic design and music production (I make music videos for events). What I can create on the Pro is just unbelievable! Thanks to great developers like Korg, Affinity, Lumafusion, the folks over at Procreate, every aspect of my creative life I used to depend on my PC for, has been replaced. In fact Affinity design and photo, and Stagelight music production are the same exact software as their desktop counterparts. Lumafusion is FinalCut Pro back on iPad. That’s how good these apps are. But you know what has not been replaced? One stupid little thing that has become the most frustrating part of moving from PC to iPad Pro? Well the one star says it all. GOOGLE SHEETS. Actually EVERYTHING GOOGLE has been the biggest problem. 

But lets start with SHEETS because that is the one application I get hired for the most in event management. I don’t really want to belittle the programming skills of Google developers but lets be real; y’all are not making software apps that handles 6 layers of 4k video and Hi end audio; Korg, Stagelight and Lumafusion does that. Sheets is zeros, ones, letters, some grid lines, fonts and some colors. That’s like one percent of what Affinity Designer deals with. Yet you guys can’t seem to give iOS users the full desktop experience most your user-base is used to in an iPad Pro? Are you serious?

Something as simple as adding coma delimitated to an email list cos you know, you can’t just straight copy your email list from Sheets to Gmail, so I need to format a split cell to accomplish this. Oh but wait, the Data menu I need to make this happen is not in Google Sheets for iOS. Why is that? I am doing my best to hold back the abusive language that’s mounting in my brain over how regressive and illogical this really is. 

Honestly Google programmers, the days of hiding behind “iPads are just not powerful enough” are long over. That excuse is gone. LONG GONE. Please update all of your Google apps to match your desktop versions. Seriously, just do it.

title: Great, but still needs features
body:
Okay— it’s not ready for five stars

I’m leaving my original review below, but the reason I am upgrading from 4 to 5 stars is that google continues to improve Sheets so much that it really is starting to compete with Microsoft Excel. I still think the Microsoft VBA capabilities are superior to the scripting in sheets (few realize how much you can do with the VBA), but I have to admit you can do some pretty cool things with google’s scripting. Also must be admitted that Microsoft has allowed Excel to become bloated and slower compared to the simple snappy interface it had years ago. I hope Sheets avoids that fate. 

====== original review =======

Very nice in terms of collaboration, but it's not Excel by any means. Since it's in development there are some obvious "seams" -- ie it's not seamless!! Examples: The mobile app has separate interfaces for viewing and editing, when you're in the editing app you can't chat with the others you're collaborating with, and since it's not Excel you can't work with Excel docs unless its the simplest of spreadsheets -- and even then you're forced to convert in order to be able to collaborate.  Hopefully one day there really will be something as powerful as (the Windows version of) Excel (including macros of course!!!) and then that will be incredibly useful with all the collaboration features Google offers. By then however Microsoft might be smart enough to move into that territory to take this away from Google. Either way I'm waiting for that day to give up my five stars!!

title: Flexible and Easy
body: Although other cloud services are available, the hidden agenda is to have you send documents In formats requiring others to buy expensive software. The flexibility of Google Suite is that documents you create can be opened by the recipients’ software to accommodate the features they may need and for which they may have paid. Create collaborative documents, share your documents, or save what you create and send it in another format: for example, create in Google Docs and send your document in a PDF format. If hyper security is your goal, I suggest you begin using distributed block chain technology not developed by the major tech companies; otherwise, most other systems can be ultimately hacked, while cloud technology is our ultimate goal for paperless. It’s time to understand the traceability of specific block chain products.

title: Good but I want more
body:
5/22/2019
Reliable app and the price is right.  My entire family of four uses it.  Sure, it does not contain all the excel features, but it also does not cost $9.99 / month time 4 family members either.  We share out college schedules and various other lists and spreadsheets.  I’ve seen investment forums share out their work because Google sheets is easy to use and so accessible.

===.===.===.===.===.===

12/15/2015 update crashes while opening existing data files.  Newly created files are ok.

If you uninstall google sheets and re-install the app, this eliminated the crashing issue for me.

===.===.===.===.===.===

I never had a problem with the app and I like that it support offline files.  I use it every day.

You data is available offline!!!

I find it cumbersome to sort or resize multiple columns.

This app works well and is free.  I share my docs with others which makes it very powerful.

title: Unable to Edit Shared Sheets
body: I try to go as mobile as possible, because opening up a computer all the time sometimes is just too much of a hassle or takes way too much time for something that should be done so quickly, such as signing up for a meeting time. Whenever I try to edit a spreadsheet for something like signing up, there’s always an annoying pop-up that says I need to download the app in order to edit at all. And even when I already have it downloaded, I still have to press the only “accept” button on that pop-up, which says “get the app”. It takes me back to the app store, where I then have to press “open”, and opens up to the Google Sheets app, but the sheets I would be trying to edit wouldn’t automatically come up. Checking the “Shared with Me” tab doesn’t do anything, trying the process over again doesn’t do anything, and nor does completely closing the App Store or Google Sheets app then starting the process over again do anything. This practically makes the Sheets app useless for me, because this is pretty much the only reason I need it. title: This is truly pathetic
body:
Is it really just me that sees a dog slow app?  I copied this review’s title from my departing comment within my effort to create a stock tracking spreadsheet. In what turned out to be my second effort at exploring using Sheets I found enormous difficulty overcoming the very long hang times and delays, so left that comment to myself to remind me in case I ever try it again. 
Add to that the fact that the stock query is missing a dividend/yield function on stocks, and we have arrived at the bizarre. That’s quite a miss.  And add to that the inability to query a closing price on a date without forcing an 5 cell array construct and we have a mess.  Apple does this in one cell with one date reference, folks. 
Well, I hate the long hanging “Calculating” times in the Numbers app, but Sheets is little better there for letting me edit while it thinks, and quite a bit more limited in overall dogginess and limitations. 
Disappointed.

title: Cheaper and more secure than network attached storage
body:
Given that most Network Attached Storage boxes are too easily hacked, I cannot justify the cost of replacing my 12 year old NAS at home.  The Google drive with Docs and Sheets is far more secure and cost effective for the long term.  I would have given Sheets 5 stars except for my continued frustration that it does not come back to where I left off.  Having to scroll down hundreds of lines every time is a waste of my time.  Other than having to learn the new formatting commands, I am very happy with Sheets.
    P.S. I was using DecCalc in the 1970s and Lotus 123 in the 1980s. I have written hundreds of spreadsheets.

title: Great free option
body:

Take the “automated” feature out, and you’ve got something!  I’m sorry that I don’t know how to turn automatic features off, and it’s annoying.

I AM GLAD to be able to make a rough spreadsheet for names, addresses and such... or, a chart that can be cut/pasted into a power point ... YES, I try to move back and forth between Google and Microsoft products, ON MY APPLE DEVICES!    

YES, you guessed it... I have ADHD-I.
But if anyone can MAKE IT WORK, it’s me!

A great product for free!  It’s Google’s FREE APPS, free e-mail, and FREE G-drive that keeps me coming back to learn more of what Google can do for me!

4 ⭐️ because I don’t like automated conversions without my permission.

title: I LOVE THIS APP!
body:
This is a great app for people on the go who use spreadsheets for work or just for at home use! It’s especially great for sports events/groups to keep track of fantasy football leagues, fantasy hockey league, etc. I love it because you can do most of the add and edit in the app without having to lug around a heavy and bulky laptop computer. One down side I saw though was there is no way to add in “Data Validation” from inside the app on Apple or Android. In order to add Data Validation I always have to go to my computer and go to Data>Data Validation to add or edit my “Data Validation” info. It would make more since and way easier if there was a way to add it, edit it, and pick from the drop down menu all in one place. It sounds easier if it’s all in one spot rather then trying to jump around through hoops and keep going back and forth between the laptop to my phone app when on the go. Other then that I love it! I hope there is a way to add this into the app. I’m hoping with the technology it can happen one day. 

I hope I made since of all this...

Once disappointment to date has been that it is either matching or lagging Microsoft Excel mostly. I say this without claiming to be an expert who has used its entire functionality, so take that with a pinch of salt.

title: Not user friendly on ipad
body:
I set up my budget to replicate an intricate spreadsheet i previously had on my laptop, but i wanted it accessible feom my mobile devices.  There are limited functions that. I wish they would add:
Fill-this is a very handy way to fill cells in a direction based on the highlighted cell (right/left, up/down) so you dont have to copy/paste your for ulas in every column.  I really wish this would be added.

Conditional formatting-this is a handy way to highlight in a different font when a cell’s value goes in the negative or when a certain threshold is breached.  Would be very helpful when managing finances.

General usage-i find i need extreme patience when using this because i have to tap once in a cell to select it, again to get the edit menus and it is just not as easy to do things.  Also, i have issues accessing my docs sometimes. 

Not my fave tool, but it gets the job done.

title: Functionality lacking
body:
All the google office or suite apps would get 5 star rating if they mirrored their website counterparts.  The functionality left out in the iPad/phone apps is a serious drawback.  As these office tools are becoming the best office group to use, it is essential that it works the same on mobile.  If one could open the online version to do the steps the app won't let you, that would help.  This too unfortunately is blocked.  If you have any of the apps installed, then you cannot access the tools online.  I considered deleting the apps and using the websites only, but then I would lose the ability to work offline.  

Google please put full functionality on your apps, or allow in app access of the desktop web version.

My concern is not limited to Apple infrastructure but also Amazon and Google. This limited functionality is a very unfair business practice, who are you to tell me what hardware i should use to access the internet or view my PURCHASED content.  Whenever i purchased a sony dvd, took it home and hooked it up to my TV.  Believe it or not, it actually plays DVDs that aren’t produced by SONY studios!! How is it not a monopoly to produce a product that only performs the functions advertised when used on a platform it chooses.  Would you buy a car that only works at one gas station? I don’t know if its Google, Amazon, Apple or all that is doing this, but I’m awfully tired of customers being the last voice in the products they get to use.  Get over it!!

I should be able to access my purchased digital media from whatever device I choose and look at all of it in the same library, regardless of where i bout it.  I should also be able to access my digital files and document, using their proper functions regardless of what device I’m using and what cloud i save too.  MY HARDWARE SHOULD NOT BE CONTROLLING WHAT DATA I DECIDE TO KEEP!!
Google Office products should have full functions on Apple and Amazon  products.  Likewise ITunes files should be able to be used on Amazon and Google products!!  Let your consumers control the property they purchase!!! Why is that a bad thing!!

Oh, and why can we not rate and review apple apps on the App Store?  You would think a company would want their customers to be able to share their opinions on its products with each other.  I’m hoping that’s just a glitch with my iPad because if not that’s pretty shady.

title: Good for when you’re in a pinch
body:

Yet, google sheets tries to get this right and mostly succeeds. You’re still going to make lots of errors and be frustrated by the nested menus of settings but the tight integration with google drive, impressive feature set and collaborative capabilities makes this a great solution for minor spreadsheet edits and reference.

title: Quasi-Functional
body:
Google Sheets (and the rest of their office products) work very well through a browser on MacOS, however with each update Google seems to be crippling the iOS versions (Sheets, Docs, Slides). Cut-and-paste with keyboard shortcuts used to work, now don't (and haven't been fixed despite several updates). Entering text in a spreadsheet cell bounces the screen distractingly up and down and then erases the contents in the cell fairly consistently. Features disappear from one version to the next.  

Unfortunately, now I cannot use iOS Chrome to access documents (I could before). I can't imagine the smart and talented engineers at Google are crippling their own iOS app, but it sure seems like it.

title: The Google experience on iOS is garbage.
body:
The Google experience on iOS is so bad it’s become unusable. Everything from their gmail app to their iOS office suite is laggy, slow, and crashes frequently. The layout is unintuitive. It does not respond like it does on web, and Google being Google, I am unable to use any of their productivity suite with iOS Safari. 

No, it’s not my hardware, it is this garbage software. Every new “update” says that they fix bugs, but it doesn’t change the fact if I tap on a cell it takes 1-2 seconds to recognize that change and will ignore the first few keystrokes I put in. It doesn’t change the fact if I insert a formula I can’t paste it into subsequent cells, I have to repeatedly rewrite the formula FOR EVERY SINGLE CELL.

Honestly it is so unusable at this point that it’s faster to import it into Excel and back. Less frustrating, too. Although Microsoft bloatware isn’t perfect, at least they have doubled down on their mobile suite. With Google, the menu options are so scattered (or completely unavailable). If their goal was to drive people to Android or the competition’s product, they’re definitely succeeding.

title: Google Holds Your Creative Work Hostage
body: I am down right angry with Google for their dishonest exploitation of many people who thought they could use Google Sheets based upon the terms & conditions that originally existed when the application was initially used. I am sure there are many people like me who have invested 100’s of hours of our creative talent developing spreadsheets within the Sheets application in order to satisfy our “personal” needs. Now that our intellectual property exists within Google’s Sheets application we are currently unable to access our “personal” intellectual property unless we sign-in to Google and by doing so agree to new terms and conditions whereby Google now owns our intellectual property and can use it in any manner it chooses. If you don’t agree to the new terms & conditions, then you CANNOT access YOUR intellectual property. So Google puts previous Sheets users in a very inferior legal position. If you want to make use of your previously created intellectual property then you must assign ownership of your intellectual property to Google who will use it as they please. If you don’t want to be robbed in this manner then you can never use your intellectual property again. Most of us who have spent many, many hours of our time developing a spreadsheet that is useful to us are usually unwilling to forego our continued access and Google takes our property for free! I firmly believe this practice was developed and implemented by Google intensionally to freely gain ownership rights to the intellectual property created by people outside of their company. Their initial marketing and roll out of the Sheets application indicated free use and no infringement upon its users intellectual property rights. But look where we are now. After trusting Google in good faith, it now appears that many of us have been swindled by a dishonest company. I will not forget this and treat Google accordingly in the future. Even the mighty Roman Empire crumbled after continuous misdeeds. I can only hope the same for Google.

title: Apple Numbers blows Google Sheets out of the water!
body:
Literally, I tried replicating a spreadsheet I use in Apple Numbers app on iOS which has a great number of tables in multiple tabs.  

Google’s sheets just can’t do it, it doesn’t come close to doing it, the app crashes consistently and I never got near entering formulae, it was crashing during the input of the text labels for the columns and rows in the table.

Seriously, people shouldn’t waste their time with absolute crap like this from Google and just use the free apps from Apple, it does everything and more that Google Sheets could, in fact Google should take a long look at how an app is supposed to work, heck Google has even made copy and paste a chore.

I now realize that my productivity is far higher on Apple Numbers than it ever could be on Sheets and Google couldn’t even claim that I am using an ancient iPad or iPhone or maybe Google just aren’t that good are developing software and apps, it seems to me that I always hear from friends about the horrendous time they are having with their Android devices and using the Sheets app on those devices too with the same terrible results.  

Googles productivity tools like sheets are designed as play things that people like Leo Laporte or Jeff Jarvis would promote using but for anyone in the real world it is just not worth even using.  Maybe their web apps are better but they won’t let me use the web apps on an iPad or iPhone...

title: I would love to love sheets...but missing features on mobile
body: Sheets is a great free spreadsheet with awesome sharing capabilities. It falls flat on the iPad/iPhone platform when you cannot reliably select multiple cells for formatting or copy and pasting. Clicking on a handle moves the handle up or down, left/right one cell, but is nearly impossible to drag and select multi cells. I've gotten it to work once, and that was on iPad Pro! Another glaring miss-step, surprising for google, is the inability to insert images into a spreadsheet from iPad/iPhone or even android! Why? You can do it on the desktop, but a simple thing like adding a logo is impossible on mobile platforms. Ironic for an app running on platform with built in camera too. Fix these things and we'll head towards true professional usability!

title: Amazingly designed and useful. Better than one would have expected for a small screen
body:
I'm a spreadsheet junkie and power user since the days of Lotus in the early 90's. 

Google Sheets on the web still has a ways to go with the feature set but it satisfies 80% of my needs, and allows me to collaborate on spreadsheets with those in my office, cross departments and entirely other companies. That alone makes this (and the rest of G-Suite) one of the most useful tools I use. 

Designing a well functioning spreadsheet app for the size of a phone screen is an incredible challenge. And I didn't expect much initially. But Google just keeps making it better. 

Sure, it's not easy to do the complex formatting, formulas and move back and forth between worksheets, but I do the heavy lifting on my laptop. The fact that I can do almost anything I need to do on my phone with fair ease is amazing. Everything is either where I would expect it to be or easily found. It might take 5 more taps than on a computer but it's all there.

title: Glaring lack of keyboard shortcuts / productivity features
body: When I write into a blank cell, the data erases after four or so characters (repeatable error), and I have to rewrite what I just entered before it sticks. Also, inexplicably absent are the command+v, c, and x shortcuts. I checked the Sheets keyboard shortcuts page. When you check out the Android version, there's something like over 20 shortcuts, quite a robust array of them. Then take a look at the iOS version of Sheets - only four shortcuts, and none of them are the essential cut/copy/paste functions. Isn't that a massive oversight for the most well-supported tablet ecosystem out there? I.e. The newest iPad 9.7 2017s are the most accessible and well-rounded tablets out there, more so than the more expensive $499 Pixel C tablet, and tablet-size scaling in apps is much better than what's currently available on Android tablets. All in all, the UX here leaves a lot to be desired, there's glitches/fritzes that are basically unheard of for an iOS app (Swift is supposed to be efficient!), and it feels as if the development for this app amounts to a half-hearted port of the Android version. Also, the way any modification changes the top bar into a long blank with a check mark to the left simply feels wrong. Microsoft Excel for iOS (which is likely newer) feels more intuitive. Currently I only stick with Sheets for certain spreadsheets that my team uses because of the APIs, but this tablet app really needs improvement.

The only thing I haven't been able to figure out is how to make rows have "wrapped text" instead of text that spills over. Perhaps that's just too many features to include for the app to remain user friendly and simple. I can always edit that when using Sheets via computer- or perhaps this feature is available via iPhone app and I just didn't figure it out yet. Overall, I highly recommend google Sheets and love google for making this available for all gmail users! Thanks!

title: Frustrating Keyboard Support on iPad Pro!

I'm a long time user of Google Apps, including the spreadsheets. It's certainly not full-featured Excel, but works pretty well as a cloud app. However, lately I've been (trying to) use it with an iPad Pro 12.9" with Apple Keyboard. It works in a pinch, but not really usable for anything long-term. You can't navigate with arrow keys. You can't tab to the next cell and then enter text in that cell without touching the screen. In other words, if you are filling out data by row, you have to touch the screen for each cell! 

I give Google Sheets on my computer 4 stars, but on this iPad Pro it's more like 1.

Edits spreadsheets pretty well, very similar to Google Sheets online.

However, this app has horrible keyboard support. I am on an iPad Pro 12.9, which a lot of people use with keyboards, myself included. This is why I am rating 2 stars. 

For starters, you cannot use the left and right arrows of the keyboard to navigate cells. Up and down work, but left right do not. That is asinine. 

Also, there are no keyboard shortcuts.... Plenty of apps have great support for keyboard shortcuts on the iPad. None of the Google Apps have any that I know of, Sheets definitely included. Command-F would be awesome to search for data. Command-C to copy whole cell data without having to select the content within the cell manually would also be great. 

How about standard text formatting shortcuts? Also not available! Would be so nice to just hit Command-B and bold a cell. Or maybe through some italics in there. Nope. Not possible with Google Sheets. Come on Google.

title: I love Google Apps, especially this one.
body: I'm not sure about anyone else's experience with Google Apps but I love them. I have had problems on occasion with my iPhone but the support has always been exceptional. Remember that iPhone(apple) doesn't always play nice in the sandbox with others and google is no exception. This product is a typical spreadsheet program much like excel. But the web based platform allows and promotes community collaboration. It is an excellent way to create and organize a bunch of people. Every year we organize a trip that includes multiple people from places all over the country. So we have an attendance tap. Then we have an equipment tab. Then we assign duties on another tap. We [the entire group] has the ability to assign tasks and report available resources. The "owner" can allow viewing or full edit capabilities. This app is awesome! And best of all, like most google products … it's FREE! So just be cautious about the whinny trolls giving bad reviews with questionable rationales. This app rocks!

title: Renewed 5 star Rating
body:
Great spreadsheet app for free! Glad it is up and running once again!

After almost 2 weeks of total dysfunctional problems after an early February upgrade, the creators have finally fixed the insurmountable looping which kept us from opening old and current spreadsheets and creating new ones! This required outdated handwritten records and desperate searches for new spreadsheet apps that might have had to been used instead. 

It would be expected that they would have tested the upgrade before rolling it out to the public and causing much unnecessary grief to its users. We  hope they have learned a valuable lesso n and will thoroughly test future upgrades prio r to release. 😉

Another star was deducted because the files don't always sync well, especially when there are new tabs created within a spreadsheet. I've had to copy paste on several occasions because what I created on my phone wasnt reflected in the desktop version and vice-versa. title: Free and incredibly useful
body:
First off, to have a program like this for free, this should truly be 5 stars. Thank you Google for this great gift.
My eyes have been opened to the usefulness of having documents like this in the cloud. Awesome for collaborating with multiple users, even in real time. Even if you just have sheet you will be updating and sharing with others, it is so much nicer than sending around new files whenever there is an update.
Sharing files is very simple and intuitive, and you can easily say if you want people to be able to just read or edit. No Google account necessary for the people you are sharing with, but if you are signed in, all your sheets are easy to access.
I think there is some room for improvement for the program generally.
The web version of the app is not great for touch input. The app is very nice for that, but that doesn't help me on a laptop using a trackpad. I'm also not as likely to be using my iPad for this program, because text entry is much easier on a computer (not the fault of the app).
One feature I would really like to see added is the ability to add padding to the cells, like you would do in a table. This would allow one to make much more readable sheets.
If you are looking for a great, free cloud spreadsheet, this is a fantastic option.

title: One important annoyance ...
body: Sheets has grown to provide excellent spreadsheet functionality across many platforms.  But unless you are using an external keyboard, this iOS version is frustrating to use because of the extra keystrokes necessary to enter numbers using the on-screen keyboard.  Also, the on- screen keyboard severely limits my view of the spreadsheet and the lack of navigation (arrow) keys is also annoying.  So, in short, although I think Sheets is a wonderful app, I give it only four starts until something is done to enhance the on-screen keyboard to include a keypad with navigation keys that do not require extra keystrokes and is economical in terms of minimizing the size of the keypad to maximize my view of my spreadsheet.  I hope future versions will address this important usability issue.

title: (Re) Pezshow; on deleted spreadsheets reappearing.
body: Pezshow comment,I hope this reaches you. The google docs & sheets, if you have a drive account, are probably still in google drive. So even though you've deleted them from you cell, they still will show up if drive is running in the background and would explain why when you open than refresh they disappear. Try turning off drive then opening spreadsheet and check if that's the case. If so then go into drive and delete the unwanted sheets from there. That's probably why they're not taking up space on your cell and nowhere to be found.

title: No complaints
body:
I have no complaints about the app's functionality. It provides me with all I need, given that what I do is fairly simple: view files which I usually edit in my desktop, occasionally edit a file lightly (edit cell content and format) and view comments. I've noticed it can do a llore other tricks but I usually prefer doing those on my desktop, but only because I find that more comfortable than editing a spreadsheet on the tiny screen of my mobile phone. 

I do have one wish, though (and it's worth mentioning it's a "nice to have"): please, if possible, make the app smaller in size. The constant updates, with such a large app (about 150 megabytes, if I remember correctly), do take some time even with wifi.

title: Sheets = Excel Lite + FREE + Anywhere
body:
Sheets is absolutely one of the coolest things google has ever produced! I can't say how happy I am with it, it's like an excel processor that I can access anywhere I have Internet.

As for down sides, it's like a lite version of excel in that it's not meant for extremely high level excel projects, it lacks a few of the bells and whistles that it has and requires a bit of shortcut knowledge to really use. Luckily the learning curve is short and easy. 

I highly recommend this to anyone who will listen, as far as personal use goes this is the best you'll probably ever need. For business's though I'd recommend a paid version of excel since you need the enterprise tools that they offer.

title: Functional, useful, easily accessible, and powerful
body:
Google Sheets helps me manage a number of things in my life -- it is amazingly useful, and surprisingly versatile.

I primarily use it for budgeting, and it serves as a checklist, so I can easily go down the list after each payday, and make sure important bills have been paid.  That way, I know where all of the money in my account is intended to go, and how much extra we have saved aside at any given time.  I create new columns for each paycheck (e.g. "1st half of month") copying them from another tab with recurring bills and payments (then I hide the columns from the past paycheck).  Usually I keep a few paychecks listed at a time.  It allows me to stay current, yet to see a bit into the future, so I can manage the current month's funds, yet not get overwhelmed.  With each current and upcoming check, I have the flexibility to add or edit rows, and to shuffle or set aside money for extra expenses.  That way I can plan for things like babysitting, money owed to friends, or cash for special occasions.  It also gives me complete control compared to fancy paid budgeting apps (trust me, I've tried them!), and I personally find it easier, more accurate, and less "squishy" (more concrete) to do it this way.

On another Sheet, I keep a detailed record of our family's credit card, home, and auto loan debt, to make sure we are on track for our goals.  After a few years of doing so, we are within striking distance of paying off a formerly very large, high interest CC balance, now at 0% rate, (due to a transfer).  I can even view graphs of our bills, debts, and monthly payments, to keep things under control.  And now we are able to pay off CCs each month and reap the rewards, instead of paying the CC companies.

I also use Sheets for managing activities (e.g., sign-up lists) for a club in which I'm involved.  Sharing a link with friends and letting them edit the document is easy.  You can also calculate and keep track of amounts of various items needed to bring to an event, or to manage volunteers, attendees, etc.

The tool is very useful, and I love that I can access it anywhere.  The web based version has a little more editing power, and can be useful when you're first setting up.  But after that, you can use Sheets on the fly to enter amounts and edit from anywhere with cell or wifi access, at any time.  I highly recommend it to anyone who wants this kind of convenience and usefulness at their fingertips.

title: Extremely disappointing
body:
I often use links to Google Sheets documents to sign up for events or volunteering opportunities. These links are usually posted on apps such as Facebook, so others can conveniently add their names to the document. However, when you open the link on the Facebook app on your phone, it asks you to download the Sheets app to edit the document. NEWSFLASH: I downloaded the app and it still will not let me edit the document on my phone! 
This forces me to have to log on to my computer in order to sign up for anything. Unfortunately, I don't always have access to a computer, so spots fill up before I get the chance to access the links on my computer. I have as a result missed out on numerous opportunities because of Google's inability to fix what is clearly a bug. I find this extremely disappointing considering the fact that this problem has existed for quite some time and appears to be a universal glitch. If I didn't have personal spreadsheets that I needed to access routinely, I would uninstall this app in a heartbeat.

body:

If you want to create a business worthy document from iOS, you'll be sorely disappointed.

Sheets is a great alternative to numbers and excel. But the iOS version is dramatically parred down. If your familiar with the desktop interface, you'll immediately see numerous features and functions are missing. This will slow you down significantly, while in some cases prohibiting you from basic features all together.

We will have to wait and see how Google leverages iPad Pro for a more legitimate desktop experience.

I start this review with a simple, personal acknowledgement that I am starting this review with a simple, personal acknowledgment. Having acknowledged that; I begin to unravel the true Pandora's box that is google slides.

It's not what can do with a simple spreadsheet app for iOS, it's what you can't not do.
Things you can do:

Interactive d&d map for real time use during skype call?(Checked)
Transform a simple calendar into a journal using notes ?(Checked)
Business stuff like slick spreadsheets (duh)

In summation you can think of sheets as a pixelated window into your soul via your smartphone or  other tablet devices.

title: Still Broken
body:
First, the app no loner loads the entire spreadsheet.  For larger spreadsheets, the process to find the bottom involves a sequence of selecting cells or zooming, scrolling, and repeating until the user finds the bottom of the spreadsheet. In previous versions, there were no issues with the app simply loading the whole of the worksheet, and the user simply scrolling to the bottom of required.

Second, the app once remembered where the user was last, meaning if you were working at the end of your spreadsheet, closed the phone, or switched tasks, then later returned, the app loaded at the last position.  Now, every time the app loads, it takes the user to the top line.  Considering how difficult it is to now get back to the bottom, this is exceedingly aggravating.

Finally, there is no longer the dialogue at the bottom asking the user how many empty rows to add at the bottom.  It has been completely removed, and the only way to add rows is to highlight one, and select insert one above or below.  This must be done individually for each new line.

All of these issues dramatically reduce productivity, and render the app for all intents and purposes, useless.

I do NOT recommend this app.

title: needs work
body:
I use three spreadsheet apps on my iPad: Apple’s Numbers, Microsoft Excel, and Google Sheets. Sheets is the worst of the three.

You can basically edit a spreadsheet in Sheets, but it really lacks polish. Here are three ways that Numbers and Excel are better than Sheets:

1. Changing the width of a column: can’t find a way to do this in Sheets.
2. When there is a Bluetooth keyboard connected, Sheets displays a big blank area on the screen where the on-screen keyboard would be.
3. No way to do a “fill” across or down.

Numbers and Excel both get these things right, and I think the desktop browser-based version of Google Sheets does too.

My recommendation: don’t use Sheets unless your spreadsheet HAS to be in Google’s cloud. Even then, consider creating it in a different app first and then uploading it to Google Drive.

title: One good feature restored... one more to go
body:
Finally with this update Google has restored one simple but critical feature: now when you scroll down a sheet and then either access another sheet or close the file, upon returning to the sheet the app will place you in the last scrolling  position you were in.  If you frequently use sheets with many rows, this is a time saver.  Sheets had this feature until several versions ago when it was dropped for whatever reason. 

But there's still one more feature missing that Sheets badly needs and actually used to have: drag to copy.  Still waiting on this one, Google.  Drag to copy... drag to copy... drag to copy.

title: Lots of changes, not all of them good
body:
I use this app almost exclusively on iPad (I very rarely access my Sheets files on PC and don't have another mobile device I can use the app on). The entire worksheet looks different!! They changed how to adjust the column widths, which you'll need to do since all the columns are wider post-update... it takes a bit of fiddling to figure out (haven't tried to alter the rows but I assume its the same). 

The font looks different. Plus, I use multiple languages in my worksheets (namely, English and Japanese), and now they're misaligned... all the kanji are floating relative to the English text and cell alignment does nothing to fix it. And, my Sheets files keep disappearing from the home screen. Only the file I use most frequently is there. Before, all my files, and files that have been shared with me, stayed in the list regardless of whether I access them or not. After each of the last two updates, those other files just disappear from my file list.

After seeing the mess updating Sheets left, I didn't even want to use this app anymore, but after cooling off a bit, it's not as bad as I first thought. I still hate the disappearing files and floating kanji, and I suppose I can wait until iOS 9, in the hope that all these horrible changes won't seem as bad after installing the new iOS. But in the meantime, I'm gonna try exporting everything back into Excel. It's gonna be a mess, but it's better than nothing. This whole ordeal may put me off Sheets for good now that Microsoft made iOS Excel free. I only started using Sheets so I could use spreadsheets on my iPad; I've been an MS Office user for decades. There's no reason not to go back to Excel anymore, depending on how good it is compared to Sheets. I'll have to see for myself.

This is great for simple to moderately advanced use. If your requirements in a spreadsheet app aren’t too complex, this will work. It is also smaller in size than Excel, helpful if you have a 16GB device.
If you have more advanced formulas or functions in your spreadsheets, pulling data from multiple worksheets for complex analysis, or multiple formulas within a cell, etc, this isn’t for you.

title: Really decent implementation!
body:
I have slowly moved over from desktop-based spreadsheets to google Sheets, and am very happy with the app. While I mostly use Sheets on my desktop computer, having access to commonly-used spreadsheets while on the go is indispensable. I can update my stock trading logs while traveling for example. They've really improved the interface from the earliest versions, and it's almost as seamless as the desktop version.

My only quibbles are the graphing function, which can be a little too presumptive about what I want to see (I.e. It gets it wrong sometimes). And it seems to bog down with giant data sets. But given the price point AND the cloud-based storage, it's a no-brainer.

No if apple would just improve the review function so the keyboard doesn't hide longer reviews! I can't see what I'm typing. 😀

As a retired accountant/programmer I have used spreadsheets as my go-to tool, from the days when Super-calc was king of the hill, through Lotus 1-2-3 and several versions of Excel. Sheets is good for general purpose use. I have no need today for higher functions like pivot tables so I don't know if Sheets includes that functionality.

The only knock I have has more to do with the platform. It is much harder to use on my iPhone than on the larger screen of my iPad and PC. That said, I love the "any platform, anywhere" idea of Sheets.

title: No .csv import support?
body:
Despite the forum help page saying .csv files are supported for import into Sheets, the truth is that they are not supported.  With almost every data download service (banks, medical, tax data) creating .csv files it is unbelievable that Sheets can import Excel but not a simple .csv file.  I spent over 40 minutes on the phone with Google before they admitted this was true and found a crazy workaround using Safari.  4 stars if .csv was supported.  5 stars if essential input functions like tab (entering a row is ugly) and cell drop-down menus were supported.

And can anyone explain how to use the full PC/desktop version of Sheets with Safari or Chrome on the iPad?  Docs works but not Sheets.

title: useless
body: This app is useless. Since we started our business 4 years ago, any Google Apps for Business user in my business was able to open multiple google spreadsheets simultaneously on an iPad with each spreadsheet opened in a different tab within Safari. This allowed us to switch instantly from open spreadsheet to open spreadsheet by simply tapping on the desired tab. Now, as we have been forced to use google sheets, we can open only one spreadsheet at a time and it opens slowly at that. To review data from a spreadsheet that is not currently open in google sheets, one must close the current spreadsheet then open the desired spreadsheet. To return to the original spreadsheet one must again close the current spreadsheet and so on and so on. This is ludicrous. The process is beyond slow and inefficient. Previously we were able to easily look at data for several different clients by quickly switching between multiple open spreadsheets with a simple click on a tab.  Additionally, the list of spreadsheets does not sort properly on the iPad. When sort by "last modified" is selected, it sorts by the last modified spreadsheets on the iPad device rather than sorting and listing the last modified spreadsheets by the user. Therefore, if the same user has used 3 different devices to modify multiple databases, google sheets only lists the databases modified on the device in use. Rubbish.

title: Increasing in functionality, but still behind the web interface
body:
While the app continues to improve in functionality and usability, there is still a ways to go before it reaches the usefulness of the web interface. I agree with many reviewers here that keyboard support would distinguish Google Sheets from its competitors. Being able to tab through cells would help with usability and some bizarre interface choices like having the cell contents come up in front of the cell being edited make me scratch my head. There also needs to be a better way to enter formulas, as you cannot just tap on cells to fill in the formula, you have to type in the cell number.

That being said, there have been many improvements to this app and I can see it going in the direction of being just as useful as Excel on the desktop.

title: Pros and Cons
body: For the most part I really enjoy using Google docs and Spreadsheet. There are pros and cons. The big plus is that I can at least function without Excel. The cons are due mostly to work-flow speed bumps, especially on mobile. For sheets larger than 4 rows/columns, you had to scroll around to find your place. title: Perfect for iPhone
body:
Great app and works well on my iPhone! I used to get so frustrated using other apps that would screw up the formatting, but when I open it later on my laptop, updates from my phone transfer to beautifully to my laptop (and vice versa). 

I correctly assumed the app would have limited editing options but was pleasantly surprised at the editing features retained and the ease of using them. Being able to freeze rows and columns is vital with all the inevitable scrolling that comes with using docs of any kind on a small device.

Even better the app lets you create new sheets, which I didn't expect at all. This way I can get basic data in a sheet on the spot and worry about fancy formatting later when I have a bigger screen to work with.

Overall user friendly app!

title: Excellent app, but could still use a few improvements.
body:
I love how simple and easy to use this app is.  I was skeptical when Google split Sheets and Docs off from the Google Drive app, but now I think it was a very smart idea.  Having the apps separate makes it much quicker and easier to find what you need because  you can just open the Docs or Sheets app and open your file directly from the recents list rather than having to navigate through all your folders just to make one addition to a spreadsheet.
The one complaint I still have is that the text in Sheets appears very small on my iPhone 5S, making it difficult to read and edit without a lot of zooming and scrolling.  Perhaps this could be fixed by just automatically scaling text size to fit the device.
Anyways, it's a great app, it's very convenient, and despite the small text I'm still very impressed with the functionality of the app.
