title: Lack of BT Keyboard shortcuts leaves much to be desired
body:
The user interface is nice and simple, very well organized. It is not as easy to use as the Apple spreadsheet or document editors, but works. 
My main complaint, and a real inconvenience, is the lack of support for the standard Apple bluetooth keyboard shortcuts (i.e. copy (cmd	+C), delete (cmd+delete/backspace), text selection (shift/ctrl + up/down/left/right), move to end of line (cmd+right - but for some reason works sometimes to the left??), etc). When using backspace to delete, each tap of the key highlights the next letter to be deleted and brings up the Copy/Paste/etc pop up. The keyboard experience is very frustrating and leaves me dissatisfied with each use. The answer provided by Google to this online is "use VoiceOver" ... that's not practical. 

Please provide BT keyboard support like even Apple Notes has (or even this review dialog box for crying out loud ... yep, tested it as I write).
author: sabatorious

title: Update ROCKS
body:
I am thrilled about the ability to passcode protect my Sheets and other Drive documents now. Previously, I had to keep my phone locked in order to protect the information in my Sheets. 

Maybe it's just me, but I would give this five stars if I could format the entire sheet based on my first formatted row. Again, I am hoping I just haven't figured it out yet, and the ability is already there. I could create and fill in my sheets so much more quickly if the program could format based on my first rows or columns of the Sheet. 

The coolest thing about Google Sheets is I can access my information no matter which device I'm using, even if it's not my own. Apple allows me to use Google on my iPhone and iPad Mini, or I can hop on at work to access all my work passwords. It doesn't matter what computer/device I'm using.  If I can get on the internet, I can access my info stored with Google. 

GOOGLE FOREVER!!!!!

title: Useable, Shareable, Good Guides
body:
I am fairly new to spreadsheet software - its been years since I used it intensively, but I was surprised to find Sheets to be really easy to use. I just took up a position as treasurer for a small organization and needed to keep track of the groups finances, and it was daunting at first. Luckily, there are plenty of guides out there for this app that cover just about everything, and the interface is pretty intuitive so you're rarely in a position of remembering where something lies in a twisted thicket of nested menus.

It also links in very easily with Google Drive, as you would expect, so once I got my spreadsheet set up it was very easy to share it with the group and keep tabs on who was doing what to it.

I would recommend this to anyone looking for a simple, easy to use but fairly feature rich spreadsheet software.

title: Pretty much unusable
body:
I don't understand the four and five star reviews. If you just need to view your spreadsheets then maybe it'll do the job. But without the ability to build formulas, this app has no hope of competing with Numbers or Excel.

Sure, I can enter formulas by manually typing them. But do you have all the formula syntax committed to memory? I sure don't. 

The formula builder in Apple's Numbers is second to none. I admittedly have not used Excel for iOS, but I can only assume that it, too, is actually designed for real spreadsheet creators.

Unless Google gets their act together and makes Sheets usable in a hurry, they can forget any hope of competing.

body:

I use Google Drive and Google Sheets for almost all my work. I'm constantly editing sheets and in the past, used the Google Drive app to do so. I loved the Drive app because I could access and edit everything on my Drive from a single app! I was willing to give the individual apps a shot, but it's been lousy.

Since being informed I could no longer edit sheets in Drive, I downloaded this app. I have had only trouble. It has crashed when I try to edit and it will not let me zoom out to view more than a few rows of a column at a time. I can't complain about anything else because I haven't been able to get any further without it crashing.

I am running iOS 7.1.2. None of my other apps have been buggy.

Google, I love Drive but I really hate this app. Please fix it.

title: Great app for chaotic thinkers, who love apps that crash!!
body:
If you're a chaotic thinker, who doesn't organize your work into logical folders and workflow, this is the app for you. You can finally enjoy sweeping through endless lists of unrelated spreadsheets searching and trying to remember which is the document you want!!! 

An added feature for those of you who love wasting time, is that this app crashes often for you!!! It can be SO boring to have apps which just work, over and over, day after day. At last, an app which keeps things interesting by repeatedly crashing, across multiple devices and accounts, for weeks on end, when you're trying to be productive and edit a spreadsheet!

If you are so unfortunate to be one to actually open a sheet, despite lack of support from Google, (I mean, who doesn't love abandonment and isolation in a technical world?!! Unmoderated forums filled with complaints are FUN to read!!) you get to experience absolutely no added benefits in features or speed from the old Drive app.

Thank you, Google, for completely hitting the mark!! For once!! Don't you dare listen to those naysayers and roll-back to a, "working" state!! ;)

title: Oh, to be misunderstood
body: I may be speaking without all the facts since I only recently began using Drive, and now Sheets.  However, I think the negative reviewers might be missing the way Sheets is intended to be used.  It is NOT a replacement for the way you currently use Drive.  It is an enhancement that allows you to EDIT what is, and SHOULD REMAIN, in your Drive.  Before Sheets, I had to do all my editing in a browser on my iPad (not smooth), or on my laptop.  Now, if I want to edit, I just open my spreadsheet through Drive, tap the edit button, and it AUTOMATICALLY opens it in Sheets for much improved editing on mobile devices.  Done?  I open the sidebar menu and click on Drive.  I don't understand all the complaints.  It's simple.  It seems the negative reviewers interpreted Sheets as a replacement for Drive when, in fact, it is an extension with augmented tools.  Just my two cents.
